key_insight: SchGen shows that PCB schematics can be generated by LLMs when the design is recast into a semantically grounded code representation instead of geometry-heavy tool syntax.
engineering_relevance: This could make PCB schematic drafting faster and more accessible by turning natural-language hardware intent into editable, connectivity-correct schematics.
method: Defines schematic editing primitives with relative placement and pin-name-based wiring.
Converts generation from geometry-driven drawing to semantics-driven matching for LLMs.
Builds a large-scale prompt-schematic dataset from open-source hardware via a human-agent collaborative pipeline.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SchGen outperforms alternative representations and larger general-purpose LLMs on wire connectivity accuracy and functional correctness.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality of the new representation and dataset coverage, so unusual component topologies or tool-specific constraints may still be challenging.
paper_title: SchGen: PCB Schematic Generation with Semantic-Grounded Code Representations
